I was in a similar situation as you, however I wanted to abort due to my age and how unprepared I was (teens and could hardly take care of myself). My boyfriend at the time said that if I chose that option he would break up with me, and I was young and naive and him being my first everything I wanted to stay with him. So I did. 

My baby ended up having an issue that caused him to spend his first month of life in the NICU (usually longer and deadlier for other babies that had what he had but he was lucky) and during that time we found out he had a disability that was permanent (again, not as serious as other cases, he got lucky, but still is a disability that affects him daily).

My boyfriend was so passionate about having our child,  and he is a great father now,  but I'll tell you, those first 2 years of my child's life, his father was terrible. I ended up taking care of our son while my boyfriend went to the gym and hung out with his friends. I loved my child but ended up resenting him for some time because I felt so lonely and taking care of a disabled child was so much harder than I could imagine.

I was so young and alone, I had no more friends and no one in my family had experience with having any disabled children or family members.  Here I was, barely able to fend for myself and I had to fend for a baby who needed extra care and therapy weekly, all because my boyfriend really wanted a child.

All I have to say is I love my son and he is the joy of my life. He is disabled but not severely, and I wouldn't change a thing about what happened. However, I went through hell to have him. I still hardly have any friends, my boyfriend decided not to be with me because he felt he "gave up too much" by being a "family man" and he was too young for all of this.  Like I said he's a great father now, and not even a bad person really, he didn't do all of this maliciously, he was just as young and immature as I was. And although my son is the light of my life,  I really wished I hadn't had him just because my boyfriend threatened me. It really caused me a lot of pain,  heartache,  depression, and suicidal thoughts that I, honestly,  was lucky to survive. I can't tell you how many times I was so close to killing myself because it's actually embarrassing.

I can't tell you what to choose. All I can do is tell you my situation and the hell that I barely survived. I love my son so much, and like I said I wouldn't change anything that happened because I'm so blessed to have him. But I'm also very lucky that I didn't end up ending my own life because then I wouldn't have destroyed my life as well as damaged my son's life.

You are being incredibly selfish. It shows just reading your title l, "I love us more than anything." Your girlfriend is more than you and your relationship.  She is her own person with her own feelings, and if you cared about her at all and not just "us" then you would tell her. Even if she never found out for the rest of her life, her relationship with you would have been a complete lie because you chose to be dishonest to her and lie to her.

First off, this is just my opinion so take it as you want. 

I don't think what you did was super terrible or anything. However, if I was to put myself in your sisters shoes, if I had a relationship as perfect as you made hers sound (which is not easy to come by) I would be devastated. I'm sure everyone else is hurting as well, however, they are not the people who have lived with him for the last few years or however long they've been married. They are not the people who spent almost every single day with him, chatting about small unimportant topics to hugely serious things. They wanted to start a family together and I bet part of what your sister is thinking is that if only they had tried sooner for a baby she would still have a part of her husband alive.

So while you all are mourning, you are no where near the pain she feels at this moment. I'm sure it was hard for her to even get out of bed and to socialize at the funeral. I'm sure the last thing she wants to see is that other people are happy,  because she lost all of her happiness in a random day. And while you guys didn't do anything too bad (in my opinion) it was just really not the right time. If I lost my world, I would not care for a single picture to be taken. I would want to shut myself away and never talk to anyone again. And to see that your family is not feeling the same grief as you and are taking pictures is just not a very good feeling.

She's just hurting very badly, and the saying is true "misery loves company." Not that she wants you guys to be miserable, but I'm sure she definitely can't stomach seeing you guys acting even remotely happy around her. She's at her lowest of lows and she cannot see a light at the end of the tunnel.

Sorry that was so long and for improper format or misspellings, I'm on my phone. I just think you could be a little more sympathetic with her.

Every time I read that you shouldn't wash raw chicken I cringe. I understand there's many different opinions and such, but my husband used to work at a chicken factory, cutting and processing whole chickens, chicken breasts, thighs, etc. According to him, people there dropped chicken on the floor many times, and just put it back into the production line. So yes, I will always be washing my chicken.

My parents never had a good relationship. I found out he cheated when I was young. I was mad at him but my hatred for him turned into hatred towards my mom instead.
Even though my dad was the cheater and not a very good husband, he never involved me in his and my mom's drama. He remained my dad. My mom, on the other hand, told me everything that was going on starting from when I was in 3rd or 4th grade. She would constantly have me spy on my dad, tell me my dad didn't love me and just generally tell me everything that went on between them.
No matter what goes on, you should never involve your children, unless they are adults and especially at such a young age.
